rounds.text: Thangamayil Jewellery Ltd demonstrates exceptional financial performance, evidenced by a compound profit growth of 42% over 10 years [E18] and 64% over 3 years [E20], alongside an astonishing 264% profit growth in the trailing twelve months [E21]. This explosive fundamental momentum is mirrored by stellar capital efficiency, with a return on equity of 28.1% [E13] and an ROCE of 25.5% [E12], significantly outperforming the sector benchmark ROCE of 9.9% [E78]. Institutional confidence is surging as foreign institutions increased their stake by 5.29 percentage points and domestic institutions by 5.04 percentage points since September 2023 [E42, E43], driving positive institutional money flow [E44]. Furthermore, the business generates substantial cash, delivering Rs 322 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 249 Cr in free cash flow in March 2026 [E35, E36], all while operating within a supportive Consumer Durables sector tailwind score of 0.72 [E75]. conceded: [E45]

The valuation of Thangamayil Jewellery Ltd is heavily stretched, trading at a Price-to-Earnings ratio of 45.9x and an aggressive Price-to-Book multiple of 12.73x against a book value of ₹ 456 [E1, E2, E72]. These multiples vastly outpace sector benchmarks, with its P/E of 51.36x and P/B of 14.18x standing well above sector medians [E6, E7]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow analysis puts intrinsic value at ₹ 5,133 per share against a market price of ₹ 5,807, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -13.1% [E45, E46]. Reverse DCF calculations show that today's price already implies an unrealistic 19.7% earnings growth rate, surpassing the base case assumption of 18.0% [E47]. Compounding these valuation concerns, promoter holdings have dropped by 5.55 percentage points over recent years, and explicit warnings highlight that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E41, E64, E65]. Conceded: the company demonstrates exceptional multi-year sales growth, high historical return on equity, and strong institutional interest [E13, E16, E42, E43].

Conceded: [E1, E2, E6, E7, E45, E46, E47, E64, E65]. While the bear focuses on stretched multiples and DCF intrinsic values, those traditional metrics miss the extraordinary operational velocity of the business, where TTM sales growth reached an astonishing 83% and TTM profit growth surged by 264% [E17, E21]. This hyper-growth easily justifies a premium valuation, especially when backed by a rules-based screen scoring a high 83 out of 100 with a BUY recommendation [E66]. Furthermore, the company's return profile utterly dominates sector medians, delivering a stellar ROCE of 23.03% and ROE of 24.83% against sector benchmarks of just 11.99% and 9.52% [E9, E10]. Far from being an isolated expensive stock, it benefits from a strong Consumer Durables sector tailwind score of +0.72 while generating substantial free cash flow of Rs 249 Cr [E36, E75]. Finally, institutional confidence is accelerating rather than fleeing, evidenced by foreign institutions increasing their holdings to 5.54% and domestic institutions rising to 16.43%, underpinned by an active positive money flow signal [E42, E43, E44].
